messages:
jared_sales: Heads-up — NovaLogic POC just started a live walkthrough and hit a bunch of 429s on /v1/generate at ~09:07 PT. They reported sudden failures when the user flow spawns 5 parallel chats. Can someone from eng look? @nina_se @ops_oncall

nina_se: Oof. Do we have the request IDs or a sample curl? Which model & max_tokens are they using? Any streaming?

jared_sales: They pasted a console dump. Model: redwood-pro-8k, max_tokens=1200, stream=false, concurrency=5. Sample error snippet below from their client:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: rl-7f3b2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 42
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "detail": "burst_token_bucket_exhausted", "retry_after_ms": 2500 }
```

ops_oncall: Pulling the gateway logs now. Standby 2m.

ops_oncall: Checked: tenant token quota is fine for the month, but their trial-tier burst window (tokens/min) was hit repeatedly due to long streamed outputs disabled and high concurrency. We also have a per-route hard cap for /v1/generate on trials at 500k tokens/min. Their combined concurrency peaked and burned the burst bucket.

nina_se: Two immediate mitigations to offer the customer: 
- Drop max_tokens to 300 and enable streaming (this reduces concurrent token holding and lets them see partial results)
- Reduce client concurrency to 2 while we temporarily raise the per-route limit for their tenant for the demo

jared_sales: They need to finish the demo in an hour. Can ops do a temporary per-route raise? If so what duration is reasonable?

ops_oncall: We can do a 6-hour temporary bump if approved. I can also apply a safety annotation (absolute ceiling) so it doesn't propagate beyond the tenant. I'll open an ops change and tag it high.

infra-bot: Ops change request submitted: CI-4720 — requested per-route tokens/min bump for tenant novalogic-77. Approver: eng-platform. ETA ~30m.

nina_se: In parallel, I'll send a short note to NovaLogic with a suggested runtime change. Example snippet to switch to streaming + reduce tokens:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-pro-8k","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":300,"stream":true}'
```

jared_sales: I'll ask them to accept that change now. If they can't, we'll wait for the ops bump. They confirmed they can toggle streaming but prefer to keep 800 tokens for fidelity.

ops_oncall: If they insist on long outputs, we should consider a fallback rule: route heavy requests to a compatible lower-SLA model variant with a higher per-route cap for the demo (e.g., redwood-xt-4k). That buys headroom with slightly different quality. Ops can orchestrate routing for the tenant temporarily.

jared_sales: Customer ok with trying redwood-xt-4k fallback if needed. Please proceed with either streaming + reduced tokens or the ops bump/reroute.

infra-bot: Manual change applied. /v1/generate per-route tokens/min = 900000 for tenant novalogic-77. Change ID: CHG-7791.

ops_oncall: Change live. Watch for X-RateLimit-Remaining in their headers. I'll tail the gateway for the next 20m and post anomalies.

nina_se: Also adding a quick note to NovaLogic about client-side exponential backoff for 429s and respecting retry_after_ms. Example pseudocode:

```
if (resp.status == 429) {
  wait(parseInt(resp.headers['retry_after_ms']) || 1000);
  retry();
}
```

jared_sales: Demo resumed and initial checks show fewer 429s. They'll monitor for the hour. Thanks team for the quick assist.

ops_oncall: One follow-up task: recommend Dedicated/reserved capacity if they plan sustained heavy concurrency. I'll add that to the post-mortem notes.

jared_sales: Noted. I'll include the Dedicated recommendation in the POC summary and next steps. Closing this thread after the demo window. :white_check_mark:
